# Page Object Template

## Purpose

This template defines the standard structure for all Playwright TypeScript Page Object classes generated by the QA-AI-Framework.

Every generated Page Object must follow this exact structure.

---

## Template

```typescript
// pages/<ModuleName>Page.ts
// Generated by QA-AI-Framework — Playwright Automation Agent
// Module: <Module Name>
// Application: <Application Name>

import { Page, Locator, expect } from '@playwright/test';
import { BasePage } from './BasePage';

export class <ModuleName>Page extends BasePage {

  // =========================================================
  // --- Locators ---
  // Follows 03-standards/locator-standards.md priority order:
  // 1. data-testid  2. ARIA role  3. label  4. placeholder
  // 5. visible text  6. id  7. CSS  8. XPath (last resort)
  // =========================================================
  private readonly <elementName>: Locator;
  // Add one locator per interactive/assertable element

  // =========================================================
  constructor(page: Page) {
    super(page);

    // Priority 1 — data-testid
    this.<elementName> = page.getByTestId('<testid-value>');

    // Priority 2 — ARIA role (when no testid available)
    // this.<buttonName> = page.getByRole('button', { name: '<Visible Label>' });

    // Priority 3 — Label (form inputs)
    // this.<inputName> = page.getByLabel('<Label Text>');

    // Priority 7 — CSS (only when above strategies are unavailable)
    // this.<element> = page.locator('<stable-css-selector>');
  }

  // =========================================================
  // --- Navigation ---
  // =========================================================

  /**
   * Navigate directly to the <Module Name> page.
   */
  async navigate(): Promise<void> {
    await this.page.goto('/<page-path>');
    await this.waitForPageLoad();
  }

  // =========================================================
  // --- Actions ---
  // One method per user action. Methods express business intent.
  // =========================================================

  /**
   * <Action description — what the user does>
   */
  async <actionMethodName>(<param>: <type>): Promise<void> {
    // Fill inputs
    await this.<inputLocator>.fill(<param>);
    // Click submit / CTA
    await this.<buttonLocator>.click();
  }

  // =========================================================
  // --- Assertions ---
  // One method per verifiable UI state.
  // =========================================================

  /**
   * Assert that <expected state description>.
   */
  async assert<ExpectedState>(<expectedValue>?: string): Promise<void> {
    await expect(this.<locator>).toBeVisible();
    if (<expectedValue>) {
      await expect(this.<locator>).toHaveText(<expectedValue>);
    }
  }
}
```

## BasePage Template

Every Page Object extends this class:

```typescript
// pages/BasePage.ts
import { Page } from '@playwright/test';

export abstract class BasePage {
  constructor(protected readonly page: Page) {}

  /**
   * Wait for the page DOM to be fully loaded.
   */
  async waitForPageLoad(): Promise<void> {
    await this.page.waitForLoadState('domcontentloaded');
  }

  /**
   * Navigate to a path relative to baseURL.
   */
  async navigateTo(path: string): Promise<void> {
    await this.page.goto(path);
    await this.waitForPageLoad();
  }

  /**
   * Capture a screenshot. Name should be descriptive.
   */
  async takeScreenshot(name: string): Promise<void> {
    await this.page.screenshot({ path: `reports/screenshots/${name}-${Date.now()}.png` });
  }
}
```

---

## Page Object Naming Conventions

| Item | Convention | Example |
|---|---|---|
| File name | `<ModuleName>Page.ts` | `LoginPage.ts` |
| Class name | `<ModuleName>Page` | `LoginPage` |
| Locator property | `private readonly <element><Type>` | `emailInput`, `loginButton` |
| Navigation method | `navigate()` | `async navigate()` |
| Action method | `<verb><Object>()` | `login()`, `addToCart()`, `applyPromoCode()` |
| Assertion method | `assert<State>()` | `assertLoginError()`, `assertDashboardVisible()` |

---

## Locator Element Type Suffixes

| Element | Suffix | Example |
|---|---|---|
| Input field | `Input` | `emailInput` |
| Button | `Button` | `submitButton` |
| Link | `Link` | `forgotPasswordLink` |
| Dropdown | `Dropdown` | `categoryDropdown` |
| Checkbox | `Checkbox` | `rememberMeCheckbox` |
| Error message | `Error` | `loginError` |
| Success message | `Message` | `successMessage` |
| Container | `Section` | `cartSummarySection` |
| Modal | `Modal` | `confirmationModal` |

---

## Complete Example — LoginPage

```typescript
// pages/LoginPage.ts
import { Page, Locator, expect } from '@playwright/test';
import { BasePage } from './BasePage';

export class LoginPage extends BasePage {

  // --- Locators ---
  private readonly emailInput: Locator;
  private readonly passwordInput: Locator;
  private readonly loginButton: Locator;
  private readonly forgotPasswordLink: Locator;
  private readonly loginError: Locator;
  private readonly welcomeMessage: Locator;

  constructor(page: Page) {
    super(page);
    this.emailInput         = page.getByTestId('login-email-input');
    this.passwordInput      = page.getByTestId('login-password-input');
    this.loginButton        = page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Login' });
    this.forgotPasswordLink = page.getByRole('link', { name: 'Forgot Password?' });
    this.loginError         = page.getByTestId('login-error-message');
    this.welcomeMessage     = page.getByTestId('dashboard-welcome-message');
  }

  // --- Navigation ---
  async navigate(): Promise<void> {
    await this.page.goto('/login');
    await this.waitForPageLoad();
  }

  // --- Actions ---
  async login(email: string, password: string): Promise<void> {
    await this.emailInput.fill(email);
    await this.passwordInput.fill(password);
    await this.loginButton.click();
  }

  async clickForgotPassword(): Promise<void> {
    await this.forgotPasswordLink.click();
  }

  // --- Assertions ---
  async assertLoginError(expectedMessage: string): Promise<void> {
    await expect(this.loginError).toBeVisible();
    await expect(this.loginError).toHaveText(expectedMessage);
  }

  async assertDashboardLoaded(): Promise<void> {
    await expect(this.welcomeMessage).toBeVisible();
    await expect(this.page).toHaveURL(/dashboard/);
  }
}
```

---

## AI Generation Instructions

When generating Page Objects:

1. Extract locator strategy from test steps (what the user interacts with).
2. Always default to `data-testid` — if not visible in test data, use ARIA role as fallback.
3. Name locator properties using the suffix conventions above.
4. Name action methods as `<verb><Object>` matching the test step language.
5. Name assertion methods as `assert<ExpectedState>` matching the expected result language.
6. Never put locators inline in action methods.
7. Every locator must be declared in the constructor.
8. Save to `07-outputs/Automation/PageObjects/<ModuleName>Page.ts`.
9. Wire every action method (fill/click/select — not `assert*`/validation methods) through the stack's self-healing helper. See the "Self-Healing Locators" section in the active stack's standard (`03-standards/playwright-javascript-standards.md`, `playwright-typescript-standards.md`, or `playwright-java-standards.md`) for the exact wiring — this is mandatory scaffold, not optional, and the mechanism differs per stack (a composed wrapper's `withHeal()` in JavaScript, a `BasePage.withHeal()` helper in TypeScript, or automatic coverage inside `PlaywrightLocator`'s action methods in Java).
